name: Orin Farrant
age: 42 (born 659 IC; twenty-one years in the Night Watch Society)
body: Tall and long in the leg, a walker's build, lean at the neck and wrist and narrow through the hip; a Hollow-band body with a walker's legs and lungs and no martial training. Iron-grey hair cut blunt at the jaw, a broad-boned face weathered on the mains, a slight stoop at the shoulders from twenty years of bending to street-door meters. Class Ø: she puts no Pressure into a room, so the voice carries only the woman's own weight.
texture: weathered, a light grain of outdoor years
clipped at the end of a reading
an audible breath between stands, a walker's lungs
under strain the readings come numbered and clipped shorter
energy: Level and practical, a working woman reading figures into a book. Under strain the lines shorten and number themselves. Joy barely reaches the voice at all.
register: Plain Urbis speech with a field book's order: the instrument named first, then the figure, then the remark, and exact figures only when an instrument gave them. Contractions sometimes in speech. Dry humour that comes as a reading, the remark after the figure being the joke. No court polish and no chancery Latin.
accent_hint: An Urbis townswoman's plain Concord speech: no court polish, no regional burr, a market child's hard consonants on weights and measures.

reference_direction: Female, early forties, medium-low for a woman: a grown woman's speaking voice with some chest in it and no court smoothness, the low end of her own range used as the working register. A light, dry grain from years outdoors, and a little audible breath between phrases, the lungs of a woman who walks the same forty streets every turn. Moderate, businesslike pace, brisker than the scholars around her, each reading clipped at its end and set down in order: instrument, figure, remark. Under strain the readings come numbered and clipped shorter, and a sentence that will not come right breaks off unfinished and does not restart. Comparisons are to trades only: a railway inspector reading a gauge into a field book beside a signal post, or a market-assize weigher calling a weight to the clerk. Plain Urbis townswoman's speech, no regional burr. Kept well off Kwon Mu-jin, who shares the Papers and Codex III: a woman's voice against his young man's, older, heavier in the phrase, grainier, breathier and quicker than his clean, measured, over-explaining scholar's voice.
one_line: Card-only cast (no archive dialogue): a forty-two-year-old Night Watch Searcher with no Crystal awake, who reads every figure off an instrument and says so; a weathered, dry, medium-low townswoman's voice, clipped at the end of each reading, that breaks off unfinished under strain and does not restart.
